extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners subject to USPTO disciplinary rules; OED staff and legal counsel handling reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and standards for imposing reciprocal discipline at the USPTO when an attorney has been disciplined by a state authority, including notice, opportunity to oppose, default consequences, and publication/notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline based on those statutes/regulations; the Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requested that the Director impose discipline identical to that imposed by the Attorney Grievance Commission of Maryland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline — being reprimanded on ethical grounds (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was found to have violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by being reprimanded on ethical grounds in the State of Maryland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: On December 2, 2009, the Attorney Grievance Commission of Maryland publicly reprimanded Respondent for violating Maryland Lawyers' Rules of Professional Conduct 1.4 and 1.7. The USPTO reciprocal proceeding rests on that out-of-jurisdiction ethical reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40-day period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. given) and was delivered to Respondent on October 17, 2011. The forty-day response window is a procedural requirement for the respondent to raise defenses under §11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (§11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline by asserting one or more of the reasons specified in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references these statutory/regulatory reasons as the exclusive bases for opposing reciprocal discipline; the page does not enumerate them but makes clear the respondent must timely invoke them in the response to the Notice and Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of failure to respond — no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined that (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and (2) a public reprimand of Respondent is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file a response under the notice procedure supports a finding that no genuine factual dispute exists and permits the Director to impose reciprocal discipline identical to the state sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of discipline imposed — identical public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: A public reprimand of Respondent is ordered; the requested reciprocal discipline is identical to the discipline imposed by the Attorney Grievance Commission of Maryland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically orders (a) public reprimand and (b) related publication and notice actions; reciprocal discipline mirrors the state disciplinary outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification obligations (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED DGC shall publish the Final Order, publish a notice in the Official Gazette, and post disciplinary decisions in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room. The OED DGC shall also give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the Respondent is admitted, to courts where the Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and provides the Reading Room URL; publication and notice are mandatory post-discipline steps to inform relevant agencies, courts, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and mailing requirements (certificate of service; §11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the most recent address provided to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certificate of service documenting mailing (date shown) is included; proper service to the respondent's last-known address is a procedural prerequisite to the disciplinary process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of practitioner registration status
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting whether the disciplined individual is a registered patent practitioner and whether authorized to practice patent law before the USPTO is part of the public notice (e.g., Mr. Hou is not a registered patent practitioner and is not authorized to practice patent law before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Notice of Reprimand includes this information to clarify the scope of the respondent's authorization to practice before the USPTO; it may affect which aspects of practice the discipline is expected to impact.
